page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at up to 3.7 GHz. The instance provisions 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. It incorporates modern vector and cryptographic instruction extensions, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI, running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Memory capacity and local I/O throughput are key specifications of this configuration. The server contains 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Bundled local storage includes 5669 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD space suitable for high-throughput scratch disks, temporary processing buffers, and caching tiers. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs and does not allocate complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark assessments highlight strong computational and in-memory execution throughput. Multi-core performance measured by stress-ng reached 147511.51 points, placing the instance in the top 10% tier of tested cloud systems, while stress-ng single-core performance attained 3077.18 points in the top 25%. In memory-centric workloads, Redis SET operations reached 112.8 million operations per second, also placing in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96ads_v6 consolidates high compute density, substantial memory, and integrated multi-terabyte NVMe storage into a single node, reducing the operational overhead of distributed fleets for large single-node workloads. Because the local NVMe storage is ephemeral, workloads requiring long-term data durability must implement remote persistent storage strategies. The configuration fits large relational and in-memory database engines, Redis clusters, enterprise analytics, transactional caches, and heavy data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, the system delivers 7.0 GB of memory per core and includes 5669 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance recorded top-tier multi-core execution on stress-ng (147511.51, top 10%) and strong single-core performance (3077.18, top 25%). High memory throughput is demonstrated by 112.8 million Redis SET operations per second (top 25%). While ephemeral local storage requires independent strategies for persistent data, the instance offers dense resource aggregation for memory-bound tasks. It is well suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise analytics, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
